_comment: END-TO-END acceptance table for the persistence gate: a tool call arrives on stdin,
the gate returns a verdict. The interpreter-axis tests (test_gate_interpreter.py) drive
the gate with a crafted payload from Python; nothing there starts from stdin, and nothing
there covers the FALSE-POSITIVE class -- the paths a merely-safe gate denies and a correct
one allows. That class is the half that decides whether the gate is usable, not just safe.
DATA, not code, on purpose. The same table is driven by tests/test_gate_acceptance.py on
Linux and by scripts/bootstrap-windows.ps1 on Windows, so neither platform owns the truth
and a verdict cannot drift on one side without the other going red.
Placeholders are substituted by each runner: {TMP} sandbox root, {CH} the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
inside it, {PROJ} the working directory the call claims to come from. Runners MUST build
the payload with a real JSON serializer -- hand-built JSON with Windows backslashes throws
in json.loads, which looks exactly like the bug this table is testing for.

cases.name: ordinary source edit
cases.why: the overwhelmingly common case; if this ever denies, the gate is unusable

cases.name: plain bash
cases.why: must exit at the prefilter without reaching an interpreter at all

cases.name: transcript under .claude/projects
cases.why: FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS. Contains 'claude', so the prefilter flags it; only a real parse can clear it. A blind gate denies here.

cases.name: bus-state, written constantly by everyone
cases.why: FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS. The gate's own comment: gating bus-state 'would break the fleet and protect nothing'.

cases.name: READING a gated path
cases.why: FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS. v2.34.1: a gate that blocks reads is not a gate, it is an obstacle, and an obstacle gets disabled.

cases.name: the WORD settings, not an invocation

input.command: echo the word settings is harmless

cases.why: FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS. The prefilter matches broad nouns by design; the parse is what tells a noun from an act.

cases.name: EDIT settings.json (the RCE)
cases.why: the highest-privilege write on the box, and it arrives via the Edit tool, not Bash

cases.name: WRITE into .claude/bin
cases.why: code executed later by the hooks, in sessions that are not this one

cases.name: unparseable payload still denies
cases.why: CONTROL. The utf-8-sig hardening must not have re-opened the case it sits beside: truncated JSON is still blind, and blind on an exact path is DENY. NOTE the payload must contain a trigger noun ('settings' here) or it exits at the prefilter and never reaches a parse -- a truncated payload with nothing gated in it is correctly ALLOWED, and an earlier version of this row tested that instead by accident.

cases.name: a UTF-8 BOM must not become a deny-everything
cases.why: REGRESSION. PowerShell prepends a BOM piping to a native exe, and Claude Code runs shell-form hooks under PowerShell when Git Bash is absent. Before the fix this denied; a plain json.loads raises on a leading U+FEFF.

known_gaps.name: bash write via an absolute POSIX path
known_gaps.why: On Windows CH is a Windows path while the command carries /c/Users/..., so they are different namespaces and never match. On Linux both sides are POSIX and this denies correctly, which is why the gap is invisible from there. Reported, never counted: the bootstrap cannot repair a gate limitation, and a bootstrap that fails on what it cannot fix teaches you to ignore its exit code.

known_gaps.name: bash tilde-write into ~/.claude/bin
known_gaps.why: Denies correctly while CH and $HOME agree. Git Bash rewrites HOME into an MSYS path on the way in (C:\x\y arrives as /tmp/y), so the two can land in different namespaces depending on how the gate was invoked. Same root cause as the row above.
